retired.note: ADR-0088 D3, the first retirement on MERIT rather than on a date. Its flag-off branch was `Adr0030PlanWorkspace`, a ~257-line second implementation of the plan surface that no shipped bundle could select and that ADR-0080 had already attributed a user-facing defect to. `plan-workspace.tsx` goes 334 lines to 24. The flag-off parity suite (plan-workspace.test.tsx) and the flag-off harness (playwright.workspace.config.ts + e2e-workspace/) are deleted with their subject (ADR-0084 D5); the splitter assertion only that harness carried was PORTED to e2e-toolbar/toolbar.spec.ts, and plan-detail.gating.test.tsx was RE-HOSTED onto the surviving layout rather than deleted — it was pen-gating coverage that merely happened to live there.

ADR-0088 D3, batch-2 retirement M1. Flag-off selected seven weekday checkboxes — a control that can say only WHETHER a day works, so it could not express the split shifts and part days ADR-0036 stores and ADR-0067 built the editor to author. Deleted with the flag: `WeekdayToggleGroup`, the `weekIsSimplified` advisory, the flag-off submit branch, and `workingWeekdays` from `calendarFormSchema` — the last because keeping a validated field with no control left to satisfy it is the ADR-0067 M4 dead end verbatim. `use-calendars.ts` keeps its `workingWeekdays` members and the flatten docblock deliberately: the API still ACCEPTS a mask, and that comment is the surviving record of why sending one is destructive. Its two `Omit<CalendarFormValues,'workingWeekdays'>` aliases were retyped — `Omit` of an absent key compiles and asserts nothing, the one site typecheck could not catch. `playwright.calendar-shifts.config.ts` is KEPT (it pinned 'true', i.e. drove the surviving world); only its one-line `env` pin went. No user-visible change: the flag was compiled on in every published image (ADR-0088 D1).

ADR-0088 D3, batch-2 retirement M2. Flag-off selected a raw `<select>` in FIVE two-arm picker sites (ActivityFormDialog, ActivityCalendarField, PlanCalendarPicker, ResourceFormDialog, ActivityResourcesPanel) and suppressed a sixth GUARD-only site (ResourceFormDialog's Group picker, whose flag-off branch was `: null` — a Class B shape, not a selection). The register said 'four pickers'; that was detect-alternative-surfaces.mjs's output, and it structurally cannot see a ternary wrapping a <div> or one behind an intervening comment — which is why the real backstop for this retirement was deleting the constant from env.ts and letting typecheck find every missed reference. `playwright.library.config.ts` is KEPT and only its ONE pin line removed: that config pins SEVEN keys including VITE_SCHEDULING_MODES:'false', so deleting the env block wholesale (the obvious 'mirror the other milestone' move) would have silently armed scheduling modes in a journey written to assert the plain surface — a live flag-off harness for a DIFFERENT flag, disarmed as collateral. No user-visible change: compiled on in every published image (ADR-0088 D1).

Its deferral trigger fired: `epic-touch: activity editor`. The register was right that retiring it ALONE collected none of the payoff — the legacy monolith would have survived as the create surface — so the dialog-unification epic closed all ten create/edit divergences and extracted eleven shared field groups first, and this retirement lands inside that epic rather than as a flag chore. Both flag-off Playwright harnesses (sub-day, assignment-lag) were CONVERTED to the shipping surface before the flag went (ADR-0084 D5), which is the ADR-0084 batch-1 lesson applied in advance. Both derived children lose their conjunct: the stranding it guarded — an editor intent with no editor to open — is now unreachable by construction.

Assertion 5 existed to stop exactly this and could not see it, because `derivedFrom` was hand-maintained and this edge had never been recorded. Both flags are Class B `keep`, so nothing was actually scheduled and the fix costs nothing; the finding is that the gate was enforcing on 3 of 9 edges. Dropping the edge instead would have been forbidden — the edge is real (env.ts:1098-1099).

deferredUntil.reason: PARKED BY THE PRODUCT OWNER 2026-08-12: every flag stays ON for now and the estate is to be cleaned up in one dedicated pass rather than a flag at a time, so the epic-touch trigger this ADR fired is superseded by that decision. The measurement stands and is why the pass is worth batching. MEASURED 2026-08-12 (ADR-0090 M6, docs/specs/workspace-layout/m6-harness-conversion.md). Seven flag-off Playwright configs pin this OFF; all seven were probed with a bare pin-flip and ALL SEVEN FAIL — 27 specs in total: base 8 of 17, activity-editor 11, edit 3, sub-day 2, notes 1, programme 1, assignment-lag 1. Not one is a configuration edit; every one needs new selectors against the surviving surface. Three of them (base, programme, notes) additionally pin VITE_TSLD_EDITING and VITE_PLAN_EDIT_LOCK off DELIBERATELY to stay pen-free, so converting those must first establish that the journey works pen-free against the surviving workspace or it silently changes what the journey tests. ADR-0090 fired the epic-touch trigger and took the milestone-s own stated off-ramp on this number rather than holding M1-M5 behind it; the trigger is re-recorded here rather than left to rot. D5 still forbids retiring before the coverage is replaced. Note sub-day and assignment-lag harness BOTH deferred survivors, so converting them is shared work whenever either is taken up.

$schema-note: enabledSource: "docblock" = the date the flag itself records; "floor" = the earliest date this repository can prove, used for the fourteen flags whose real flip is recorded NOWHERE (ADR-0084). A floor can only make a flag look YOUNGER than it is, so retiring on one is conservative — never premature. It is not corrected by guessing.
sizing:
A batch is sized by BLAST RADIUS. The enablement cohort only sets the EARLIEST date a flag may fall on (enabled + horizonDays); it does not set the batch. Re-spaced 2026-08-09 after the original cohort-only split put 17 flags and ~75 production files into a batch due in nine days — the largest batch on the second-earliest date.
MEASURED per flag: production files referencing the constant, and the number of playwright*.config.ts files that PIN it. The pin count is the one nobody had: VITE_CANVAS_AUTHORING is pinned in 14 configs and VITE_SCHEDULING_MODES in 13, and CI proved a single pinned config costs six specs to convert, not a line.
ESTIMATED, and labelled as such: weight = files + 3x pins and a cap of 45 per batch. The cadence was fortnightly and is WEEKLY from batch-2 (product owner, 2026-08-09), which finishes the queue 2026-12-01 rather than 2027-03-23. Note what that does to the estimate: the batch COMPOSITION was fitted against a fortnight and now has a week, so the cap is the part now under test — halving the cadence doubles the rate of work without re-sizing a single batch. The weighting, the cap and the cadence all come from ONE completed retirement, so they are a hypothesis rather than a plan. `check:flags` tests it for us — if batch 2 takes longer than its week, the next batch date fails and forces a re-fit against a second data point. Re-fit it then; do not defend it.

classA.VITE_CANVAS_WORKSPACE: Selects <PlanWorkspace> or <LegacyPlanLayout>, the pre-ADR-0030 stacked plan-detail page. Harnessed by seven configs — the largest conversion cost in the estate, and the register carried NO note for it until ADR-0088 D5.

$classA-note: ADR-0088 D2/D3. Authoritative — `scripts/detect-alternative-surfaces.mjs` is a TRIPWIRE that asserts `detected subset-of classA`, never the converse, because it can only under-detect (a flag branching by early return, by `const B = FLAG ? X : Y`, or through an indirection is invisible to it and is legitimately curated by hand). `classACap` is the MEASURED count and ratchets DOWN after each retirement; raising it needs an ADR.
$flag-cleanup-note: `flag-cleanup pass` was added to the vocabulary on 2026-08-12 by product-owner decision, which is exactly the form the note below asks for — a decision somebody makes, in a diff, rather than a free-text sentence in one flag's reason. It supersedes `epic-touch: plan workspace` for VITE_CANVAS_WORKSPACE: ADR-0090 FIRED that trigger and measured the cost (all seven harnesses fail a bare pin-flip, 27 specs), and the owner's call is that every flag stays ON and the estate is cleaned up in ONE batched pass rather than a flag at a time. That is a stronger reason than the epic's own off-ramp, and it is a real event rather than an indefinite opt-out — but note it is also a WIDER one, so a second flag deferred under it should be a deliberate choice and not a habit.
$deferral-note: ADR-0088 D3a. A Class A flag may be deferred past its batch date, but NOT by a bare date and NOT by `keep` — `keep` means 'Class B, guard-only, never retires', which is a written false statement about a Class A flag and corrupts the classification this register exists to defend. A deferral carries a trigger from `deferralTriggers` (a CLOSED vocabulary: adding a value is a decision somebody makes, in a diff) and a named TECH_DEBT row, so it is an event that will happen rather than an indefinite opt-out. This is the escape hatch the epic exists to remove, so it is bounded by construction.
